title: Int8 overflow silently corrupted session labels
body: Polars returns dt.hour() as Int8, so hour*60 wrapped (09:30 ET became minute 58). Every NYSE-open / CME-weekend flag would have been wrong, and every weekend hypothesis would have been tested on garbage without any error raised. Caught only because the DST unit test pinned exact UTC instants. Fix: cast to Int32 before arithmetic. Lesson: any time arithmetic in polars needs an explicit cast, and calendar logic needs tests at known instants (both DST regimes).

title: Weekend completeness filter used a full-sample statistic
body: weekend_table first dropped incomplete weekends using the median weekend length over the whole sample: a full-sample statistic, i.e. subtle look-ahead. Replaced with a causal check (a non-weekend bar exists after the weekend). The causality test now compares a truncated frame against the full frame.

title: Evaluator sizes at entry and holds; no-trade band 0.2
body: The first version re-sized every bar as s/sigma, which charged rebalancing costs every time sigma-hat drifted, even with a constant signal. Real trades are sized at entry. Policy now: notional fixed at entry and re-sized only on a sign flip, going flat, or |signal change| > 0.2. Continuous-signal strategies (tsmom, ema_stack) still pay for genuine conviction changes. This choice affects every cost number in the playbook, so note it when comparing strategies.

title: Research split at my knowledge cutoff (2026-07-01)
body: Hypotheses I propose about pre-cutoff data may be recall of trader lore, not discovery. Every result is therefore reported as llm_in_sample vs clean_holdout (>= 2026-07-01, ~4 months so far). A verdict needs the holdout to keep the in-sample sign. Expect most early verdicts to be inconclusive; that is the honest outcome.

title: Bybit lists TradFi perps; universe filter added
body: atx universe first included SOXL, MU, SPCX, XAU, WTI perpetuals (symbolType ETF/stock/commodity). Now excluded via universe.symbol_types. Worth revisiting: XAUUSDT and stock perps trading 24/7 on Bybit are a direct read of weekend TradFi sentiment, and could serve as the information proxy H-W3 needs.

title: H-W5 test as specified is biased by sigma standardisation
body: H-W5 compares |z| in the Monday NYSE-open window after eventful weekends with other days. But z = r / sigma_{t|t-1}, and the EWMA sigma has already absorbed the weekend shock by Monday, so Monday's z is deflated exactly when the weekend was eventful. Early number (3 symbols): ratio 0.67, which looks like a 'contradiction' but is mostly this artefact. Not fixing H-W5 in place (that would be data snooping). Registering H-W5b, which normalises the Monday-open moves by the pre-weekend sigma (sigma_fri), as a separate trial.

title: Weekend study (1h, 23 symbols, 344 weekends): vol yes, direction no
body: H-W1 SUPPORTED both segments: weekend realised vol is ~0.77x the Friday-implied level (median rv_ratio 0.77 in-sample, 0.82 holdout; 78%/83% of weekends below 1). H-W5b SUPPORTED in-sample: after eventful weekends (|wk_z| >= 2), Monday's NYSE-open window moves 1.43x a normal open (CI 1.25-1.65); holdout 1.94x, but only 6 weekends. Direction is NOT supported: H-W3 (follow information shocks) has the wrong sign (-0.08, t -0.3); H-W2 (fade low-activity drift) has the wrong sign in-sample (+0.12) but the right sign in holdout (-0.24, t -1.4); H-W4 (CME gap fill) shows no excess over the random-walk null in-sample (-1pp, t -0.8). Reading: the TradFi reopen is a *volatility* inflection point, not a predictable *directional* one at this resolution. Practical use now: widen stops / reduce size into Monday's NYSE open after eventful weekends, and don't trade gap-fill lore. To find directional weekend edge we likely need an information proxy (news volume, TradFi perps on Bybit, CME basis), not just price and turnover.

title: Shocks: calm-market shocks continue, liquidation shocks reverse
body: My pre-registered H-S1 was wrong: I expected continuation in R3/R9 and reversal in R4/R5. In-sample it's the reverse: R1 +0.14 (t 3.8), R4 +0.09 (t 3.3), R9 -0.23 (t -4.5) signed 24h z after |z| >= 4 shocks. Registered H-S2 (data-generated) and checked the holdout: supported (R1 +0.45 t 2.8, R4 +0.18, R9 -0.07). The holdout also showed reversal in every normal/high-vol cell (R5 -0.25 t -3.0, R6 -0.20 t -2.1, R8 -0.19 t -2.0). That became H-S3, which is only testable on data after 2026-11-08, since I found it in this holdout. Interpretation: a big move into a quiet book is repricing on information; a big move in an already-volatile book is forced flow that exhausts. This maps directly onto the playbook: continuation setups after shocks in R1/R4/R7, fade setups after shocks elsewhere.

title: Strategy x regime at 1h: costs and trend dominate; mean reversion fails
body: Gross vs net decomposition (8 majors, in-sample, risk units x100 per active bar): ema_stack +0.61 gross / +0.45 net; donchian +0.65 / +0.41; tsmom +0.53 / -0.05 (continuous signal, turnover eats it); rsi_reversion +0.06 / -0.80 (no edge, all cost); zscore_reversion -1.54 gross (genuine anti-edge: 2-sigma hourly deviations keep going). H-T1 (registered after seeing this) holds in the holdout: zscore gross -3.2. H-R1 and H-R2 fail as stated: the by-cell sign patterns are noisy at 1h and trend strategies are negative in the holdout's R9 (late-2026 liquidation episodes). Lessons: (1) turnover is the first-order driver at 1h, so playbook priors must be net of costs and probably evaluated at 4h too; (2) mean-reversion priors for crypto perps should be weak at intraday horizons; (3) the v0 labeller may be too noisy to separate cells (cell results flip sign between segments). Next: compare with the factorial HMM labeller.

title: Forward-path priors are nearly symmetric; R7 skews down, R9 bounces
body: 24h forward paths in sigma units: medians ~0 in every cell, MFE ~ |MAE| ~ 2.5-4 sigma. So vol-only TP/SL placement carries no free edge (as the first-passage maths predicts). Exceptions: R7 (grind down) mean -0.14, MAE -4.2 vs MFE +3.3, so downside continuation and asymmetric risk; R9 (liquidation) p_up 0.56, median +0.10, a bounce tendency. Both consistent with H-S2's 'liquidations exhaust'. Use: for TP/SL, the structural level chain must supply the edge; the regime only tilts drift.

title: For the user: information proxy for weekend direction
body: Weekend vol and Monday-open vol effects are real, but direction isn't predictable from price/turnover alone. Candidate information proxies, all available now: (a) Bybit TradFi perps (XAU, stock perps) trading through the weekend; (b) GDELT news volume spikes during the weekend; (c) funding/OI build-up over the weekend (backfill in progress). Which do you want to prioritise?

title: Weekend strategies never traded: Sunday counted as 'absorbed'
body: wk_absorbed used weekday > 1, so Sunday (weekday 7) after the 18:00 ET reopen was treated as past Monday's close, and every entry was cancelled on the bar it fired. All three calendar strategies showed zero trades in the first 1h playbook. Tests passed because they checked causality and flatness but never that the strategy trades at all. Fixed (Tue-Sat or Monday >= 16:00 ET) and added the missing test. Lesson: every strategy test must include 'it actually produces positions on a sample where it should'.

title: Applied data-audit fixes before trusting results
body: Audit agent findings: BCHUSDT 1d 2020-12-14 has open = low = 0 (venue data); 1,037 identical duplicate rows from my overlapping test ingests; 2020-21 4h/1d volumes disagree with 1h sums; listing days are pathological. Applied: price-sanity filter (Python frame + Rust kline ingestion), listing burn-in of 14 days (30 for 2023+ listings), deterministic tie-break in read_asof (latest file wins). Research uses 1h bars, so the pre-2022 4h/1d mismatch doesn't touch these results yet. The rerun after the fixes reproduced every verdict.

title: Order-flow storage = 3 s candles only; everything else derived
body: Raw L2 deltas are tens of GB/day, so the collector aggregates in memory and stores 3 s candles: taker buy/sell volume and notional (V and Delta derived), time-weighted spread / microprice / OBI at 5-100 bps bands / depth at 25 and 100 bps, summed L1 OFI, plus quality columns (book span, coverage). 1 m rollups are exact; SMA / EMA / EMA-of-SMA stacks and z-scores are computed on read. Budget: rolling 3 s window + permanent 1 m tier, pruned oldest-first and only after rollup.

title: Book depth 200 is useless for % bands on BTC; 1000 needed
body: BTC perp with orderbook.200 spans only ~4 bps from mid, so every OBI band 5-100 bps was identical (truncated). With orderbook.1000: BTC perp ~28 bps, BTC spot ~93 bps, ETH perp ~65 bps. Alts reach 200+ bps even at depth 200. Bybit linear offers 1/50/200/1000 (500 doesn't exist). Every band beyond book_span_bps must be treated as missing, so the span column is part of the schema.

title: Exchange clock ahead of local: known_ts before candle end
body: First collector test: median (known_ts - event_ts) 2.8 s for 3 s candles. Bybit's clock runs ~0.3 s ahead of the local clock, so a candle closed by a later exchange event got a local known_ts before its own exchange-time end. That's a small look-ahead. Fixed: known_ts = max(local finalisation, candle end).

title: Changed the schema while a backfill was running
body: I added the f32 column type to config/schema.yaml while the research backfill still ran an older binary that re-reads the schema per command. The last step (ETH trade flow, 180 days) failed on the unknown type. Rerunning with the new binary. Process lesson: never edit the shared schema contract while long ingestion jobs are running; or version the schema.

title: Bybit catalogue: TradFi perps trade all weekend; most perps have no spot
body: 937 linear instruments (310 TradFi perps: 243 stock, 59 ETF, 4 commodity, 4 forex; 7 pre-listing perps on private companies, e.g. ANTHROPICUSDT and OPENAIUSDT), 521 spot pairs, 6,872 options on 16 underlyings (incl. NVDA, TSLA, QQQ). 307 of the 310 TradFi perps traded on a Saturday, and SOXLUSDT does ~16M/day. That's the weekend information proxy H-W3 was missing: a weekend move in crypto that coincides with a move in weekend-traded stock/ETF perps is plausibly macro information, not thin-book drift. 217 of 408 crypto perps have no Bybit spot pair, so spot-vs-perp flow (H-F3) is limited to the top names.

title: Live order-flow collection started: 70 streams, ~120 MB/day
body: Collector live since 2026-11-07 18:05 UTC: 48 linear perps (BTC/ETH at depth 1000; Tier A + Tier B crypto + 13 TradFi perps at depth 200) and 20 spot pairs (BTC/ETH at depth 1000). First flush: 70/70 streams, ~99% book coverage, 0 reconnects. Measured 59 B per compacted 3 s candle, i.e. 1.7 MB per stream-day, so about 200 days of 3 s data fit the 30 GB budget, alongside a permanent 1 m tier. Every flow hypothesis (H-F1..F4, H-W6) was registered before this data existed, so all of it is clean holdout for me. To watch: ZEC's depth-200 book spans only ~20 bps (raise to 1000?); BEAM spot is thin (12 bps spread).

title: Prior projects: two serious efforts, almost no deployable edge
body: ETH_BMNR: 15 strategy families, 0 deployable (mNAV premium no edge; BMNR too illiquid; pairs 0/10,080 survive deflation; OBI alpha real at 1 s but below costs). TREND_FOLLOWING: champion Sharpe 0.8 came from ~300-500 configs over 13 LLM-agent rounds that reused the 'OOS' half every round; the live rule on truly unseen 2020-22 data has Sharpe -0.12. Only a pre-registered hedged short strangle survives (deflated Sharpe 0.57). This is exactly the failure mode AI_Trader's protocol exists for, now written into the protocol as explicit rules.

title: H-W7 supported: options overprice TradFi weekends by 2-5x
body: Realised variance over Fri 17:00 -> Sun 18:00 ET vs variance implied by Friday 08:00 UTC 7d ATM IV (imported Deribit SVI): BTC 0.35x (in-sample, 326 weeks) / 0.20x (holdout, 15 weeks); ETH 0.45x / 0.27x. Weekday windows of equal length: 0.84-0.97x. Difference t = -17 / -7.7 (BTC), -15 / -5.3 (ETH). The strongest, cleanest effect so far, and it holds post-cutoff. Uses: weekend sigma ~0.5-0.6x Friday sigma for stops, sizing and first-passage; candidate weekend short-vol sleeve on Bybit options (needs cost and tail study: weekend jumps are exactly where short vol dies).

title: Two test-design errors in one hypothesis (H-X2)
body: (1) Compared per-day P&L in bar-risk units across 1h/4h/1d: not scale-free (a 1h position carries ~5x the daily risk). Invalidated and re-registered as H-X2b with Sharpe. (2) Then filtered the frame to the holdout BEFORE computing signals, which restarted indicator warm-up (1d had no signals at all: NaN). Corrected: signals on full history, P&L split by date. Result: 4h beats 1h in both segments; 1d doesn't, so the registered verdict is 'contradicts'. '4h sweet spot' is registered as H-X2c, forward-only from 2026-11-08. Both rules are now in the protocol.

title: Imported validated data from prior projects
body: Into the lake: Bybit BTC 5m 2020-04 -> 2026-09 (matches our 1h exactly from 2022; 2021 venue-vintage mismatches as in the audit), Binance ETH 1h (2017->) and 1m (2023->), Deribit BTC/ETH perps 1h, Deribit funding 2019->, Deribit SVI surfaces 2,474 days (ATM / RR25 / BF25 at 7/30/90d). Lake now 0.31 GB. Not imported: survivor 50-coin bars, a results file with account metadata, 3-day L2 samples.

title: H-S4 supported: EWMA over-forecasts post-jump vol by ~27%
body: 1h, 23 symbols, |z| >= 5 jumps declustered over 24h: excess variance (vs the pre-jump sigma^2) is ~9.7x in hour 1, ~3.9x by hour 6, ~2.3x by hour 24; half-life 3 bars in-sample (3,396 events) and 2 bars in the holdout (253). Realised 24h vol / EWMA forecast made right after the jump: median 0.73 (both segments). Implication: the lambda=0.94 EWMA lets one jump inflate sigma too much, so post-jump stops and sizing are too conservative and H-S2/S3 reversal setups get under-sized. Next: a jump-robust sigma (winsorised or bipower-variation input to the EWMA / GARCH-t) as a vol tool, validated against this event study.

title: H-X3, H-P1, H-P2 not supported; positioning strategies have no in-sample edge
body: H-X3: cross-sectional rank IC of RV20 percentile vs next-10d trend P&L ~0 (tsmom -0.03 t-1.7, ema_stack -0.01, donchian +0.03); the prior project's -0.19 was a time-series IC on one book, a different question, and I'm not re-slicing it. H-P1 funding_contrarian at 4h: pooled -1.7 (x100, t -1.5) in-sample and +5.5 (t 1.2) in the 4-month holdout; registered verdict contradicts. H-P2 oi_price_divergence: ~0 pooled, no better than buy-and-hold. Funding/OI as standalone 4h signals: no. They may still matter as context (crowding) for the regime / shock layer.

title: H-X1 not supported: keep resting stops
body: BTC 5m simulation of structural stops (agent-built research/stops.py): close-confirmed + 2x catastrophe stop vs resting stop. ema_stack n=299 in-sample: B-A -0.046R (t -0.95); donchian n=17: -0.048R. About half of resting-stop touches do close back inside the hour (52-64%, so the prior project's observation replicates), but the close-confirmed losers are larger (worst -1.9R vs -1.0R, ~12% hit the catastrophe stop). Decision: at-exec keeps resting SL with the MarkPrice trigger. Design issue found: breakout entries sit a median 6.3 sigma from the last pivot, so placement.max_stop_distance_sigma = 4 rejects 95% of donchian entries. The cap and the breakout strategy are incompatible; revisit when the placement layer is built.

title: H-W6 untestable as designed: TradFi perps freeze over weekends
body: Bybit stock/ETF perps barely trade on TradFi weekends: weekend realised vol ~0.21-0.32x the Friday-implied level, turnover 0.1-0.2x weekdays, max |weekend z| < 0.75 over ~20 weekends (listed Apr-Jun 2026). They track an index that's frozen while the underlying is closed, so they carry no weekend information; zero 'confirmed' weekends. My catalogue-based idea was wrong. Side observation: crypto weekend moves of |z| >= 1 reverted by Monday's NYSE close in the holdout (mean signed -0.38, 17 weekends), consistent with H-W2's holdout. Weekend information proxies left to try: GDELT news volume, Polymarket moves, on-chain flows (not stock perps).

title: Vol tools: robust + bias-corrected EWMA validated; weekend shrink only for central estimates
body: H-V1 (winsorise at 4 sigma) FAILED: post-jump calibration fixed (0.97 vs 0.73) but QLIKE worse (+0.006, t +2.5), because clipping biases variance down (in-sample weekday windows under-forecast, median realised/forecast 1.05). H-V1b (registered from in-sample diagnostics only) adds a slow bias factor EWMA_0.999(r^2)/EWMA_0.999(clipped^2): SUPPORTED, dQLIKE -0.051 (t -8.8) in-sample and -0.039 (t -3.6) holdout, post-jump ratio 0.92. H-V2 (weekend scaling) FAILED on QLIKE for weekend windows (+0.018), even though median calibration improves a lot (pure-weekend windows 0.62 -> 0.75). Weekends are quiet in the median but jump-prone, so shrinking sigma turns the rare weekend shock into a big under-forecast. Design decision: two sigmas. sigma_risk_next (no weekend shrink) for stops and sizing; sigma_rb_next (weekend-scaled) for central estimates (first passage, TP probability). Live now: BTC m = 0.57.

title: shock_regime strategy built; forward-test only
body: Agent-built strategies/shock.py: on |z| >= 4 shocks (24-bar decluster), continuation if vol_state is low at the shock, reversal otherwise; size min(1, |z|/8); continuation exits on a full retrace of the shock bar or a 2-sigma trailing close stop; reversal exits at the shock bar's open (target) or beyond its extreme + 0.5 sigma (invalidation). No time exits. BTC 1h history: 526 trades (64% continuation), in position 14% of bars, median 10 bars. P&L deliberately NOT inspected: the rule was designed after seeing the in-sample evidence, so only results from 2026-11-08 on count (H-S3).

title: Vol clustering is multi-scale: HAR beats the robust EWMA at 24h
body: H-VCL1 SUPPORTED both segments: HAR on log daily RV (1d / 7d / 30d components, expanding OLS refit monthly, lognormal correction) vs robust_bc 24h forecast: QLIKE 0.380 vs 0.462 in-sample (dQLIKE -0.079, t -7.4, 2,094 days) and 0.415 vs 0.502 in the holdout (t -2.5). Long-memory clustering matters at daily horizons; the single-lambda EWMA is right for per-bar intraday sigma, not for the daily risk forecast. H-LC2 NOT supported: after Amihud illiquidity spikes (log z >= 2), realised 24h vol was BELOW the forecast (median 0.87, CI 0.75-0.99, 74 events): illiquidity spikes here are mostly quiet, thin periods, not crunches. Liquidity crunches need book data (depth collapse in flow_3s), not bar-based proxies.

title: sigma_risk_next wasn't the validated model
body: When wiring the vol tools I took sigma_risk_next from the weekend-seasonal model's base variance, not from the exact configuration validated in H-V1b (robust + bias correction, no weekend). Caught while setting up H-LC2; fixed by running the validated configuration separately in add_robust_vol. Lesson: a tool label must point to the exact validated configuration, never a near relative.

title: Vector candles: no exploitable edge in direction, zones or vol
body: 15,333 in-sample and 1,203 holdout declustered 1h vector candles (range >= 3 sigma, turnover >= 2x the weekly median, body >= 60%). H-VC1 continuation: none at 24h (-0.005, t -0.3). H-VC2 zone revisit: real but small excess over the reflection null (+3pp IS, t 7; +4pp holdout), below the 5pp bar. H-VC3 'zone as S/R': my design was flawed (near edge = the vector's own close, touched immediately); the first 1-sigma move breaks through slightly more often (52-55%). H-VC4 vol clustering after vectors: no (realised/robust forecast 0.92 vs 0.94 after plain jumps). H-VC5 aligned taker flow: no difference (small n). What survives as forward-only candidates: thin vectors revert (H-VC6), the first move after a vector goes against it (H-VC7). Honest read: the 'vector candle' lore doesn't survive proper nulls on 1h crypto bars; whatever is real lives at finer resolution (flow_3s) or in thin-print cases.

title: H-VC3 measured the wrong thing (my definition)
body: I defined the zone's 'near edge' as the close side of the body, i.e. the vector candle's own close, so every event 'touched' it on the next bar and the test reduced to the direction of the next 1-sigma move. A proper S/R test needs a level price has moved AWAY from first (e.g. require a 1-sigma excursion beyond the edge before a touch counts). Recorded the verdict as registered; the actual measurement became H-VC7 (forward-only).

title: Vector-open levels (4h, active until taken) don't hold; they break slightly more than chance
body: User's construct (chart 2026-11-07): 4h vector candle OPEN as a level, active until first taken by a wick/body, expected to act as S/R on that first touch and switch off afterwards. PVSRA climax definition (vol >= 2x avg10 OR vol*range = max of 11), 23 symbols, 28,302 first touches in-sample / 2,213 holdout, per-event driftless null from the touch close (handles wick touches). First-touch rejection minus null: -1.6pp (t -4.0) in-sample, -2.6pp (t -1.8) holdout; worse than ordinary candle opens (-0.8pp / -2.9pp); no clear 'switched off' pattern; no magnet effect beyond the reflection null (+0.1pp / +1.0pp). Same direction as the 1h H-VC3/H-VC7 observation: price tends to go THROUGH these levels slightly more than a random walk. Belief for the level chain: vector-origin levels get break probability >= 0.5, not < 0.5. Caveats to discuss with the user: (1) their chart is Coinbase spot BTC, ours Bybit perps across 23 symbols; (2) their indicator's vector rule may differ from PVSRA; (3) visually chosen examples are prone to selection bias (memorable rejections). If their exact indicator rule is available, it should be registered as its own hypothesis.

title: Pivot geometry (user's indicator): no edge beyond slow trend; DC stops far beyond the 4-sigma cap
body: Faithful port of the Pine 'Pivot geometry trend' (DC pivots, K-ensemble 3/4/6/8/12, no selection). 4h, 23 symbols, mean annualised Sharpe in-sample / holdout: geo_struct -0.04 / -0.90, geo_pivot_bo 0.31 / -0.60, geo_flag_bo 0.06 / -1.16, geo_avg 0.16 / -1.03 vs ema_stack 0.24 / -0.43, donchian 0.28 / 0.02, tsmom 0.36 / -0.56; geo_avg correlates 0.72 with ema_stack. Replicates the prior project's conclusion on 20 new symbols: a noisier copy of slow trend. FLAG_BO structural stops at entry: median 6.0 sigma (K=6: 8.2), 84-98% beyond our 4-sigma cap, so DC structure and the cap are incompatible (same conflict as H-X1's donchian finding).

title: H-GT3 used the wrong null (I'd fixed exactly this in H-VZ1)
body: I registered H-GT3 against a flat 0.5 null, but the race starts at the touch bar's close, which is usually already back on the original side (only the wick touched). The proper driftless null is ~0.55-0.57; vs that, the 0.574 rejection rate is noise (z ~ 0.8). The mechanical verdict said 'supports'; I appended a correction record. Rule: every level-reaction test uses the per-event null from the race starting point, never 0.5.

title: First decision walk-through on live state (Sat 2026-11-07 21:00 UTC)
body: State: BTC/ETH/SOL in R7 grind down at the 9-14th vol percentile; XRP R8. TradFi weekend 24h in: BTC -0.10 sigma, realised 0.26x Friday sigma (ETH 0.30x). Implied vs HAR forecast: BTC 1.19x, ETH 1.39x, before the weekend discount (m 0.57-0.68). Last shocks Thu 15:00 (-5.1 / -5.4 sigma) in high-vol cells -> S2 fades; ETH's still open (entry 2,251, target 2,342, now 2,231). My calls: (1) the edge tonight is volatility (weekend short-vol, S3), but there's no options sleeve yet so it's a note, not a trade; (2) no new directional entries over the weekend; (3) keep the ETH fade per its rule; (4) small trend-short tilt; (5) for Monday, vol is low, so any 4-sigma shock = continuation (S1), not a fade. Found while doing this: bars aren't refreshed live (stale 6h), so a bar updater is needed before any live session; and the HAR tool had a NaN-propagation bug (fixed + test).

title: Vol / fundamentals / carry batch: carry real but decayed; most vol add-ons fail
body: H-C1 SUPPORTED: perp funding carry (short perp / long spot, 7d sign filter), net Sharpe 2.76 in-sample, but decaying by year: 24% (2020), 57% (2021), -2.7% (2022), 7% (2023), 11% (2024), 0.5% (2025), -4.8% (2026 H1); holdout +1.2%/yr. The filter's turnover eats 2/3 of today's gross carry, and after capital cost it's below cash. It's a regime-dependent premium (big in leverage manias), not a standing one; registered H-C1b (always-on, funding-scaled overlay) forward-only. H-VCL4 implied vol adds to HAR: QLIKE -3% in-sample (t -1.4, inconclusive), -19% holdout (t -2.0): use DVOL as a feature for BTC/ETH risk. Not supported: H-VCL2 downside semivariance (no leverage effect at daily HAR level), H-VCL3 BTC->alt spillover (alts' own HAR already captures it), H-VCL5 compression (no extra expansion vs HAR), H-FU1 stablecoins, H-FU2 VRP -> returns (in-sample negative slope; holdout positive on ~3.5 independent observations = noise).

title: H-VCL5 success criterion was unreachable
body: I required median(realised/HAR forecast) > 1.1, but HAR's forecast is a lognormal MEAN (exp(mu + s2/2)); with right-skewed RV, the median ratio sits around 0.7 for ALL days. The test should compare compressed days against the all-days baseline (same metric), which the agent reported: -0.270 vs -0.280 mean log ratio, i.e. no difference. Conclusion stands (no compression effect), but the criterion was badly specified. Rule: ratio tests must be relative to the unconditional baseline of the same metric.

title: Auction / regime-switch batch: value areas and variance ratio don't tell trend from mean reversion
body: BTC 5m-built daily volume profiles (ETH 1m as in-sample replication), decisions on 1h. H-AU1 acceptance outside value -> continuation: raw +0.13 sigma (t 5.2) but a random walk through the same levels gives +0.09 (my 'one event per day' design leaks look-ahead); excess +0.04 sigma (t 1.6), ~12 bps: below costs. H-AU2 '80% rule': 34% vs 36% null. H-AU3 balance/imbalance DiD ~0 (trend beats MR by the same margin in both). H-AU4 prior POC magnet: +1pp. H-RG1 variance-ratio regime switch: DiD ~0 over 5,619 symbol-weeks. Conclusion: market-profile levels behave like random-walk levels; neither VA overlap nor VR switches between trend and MR. The only stable fact: 1h MR as configured loses everywhere net of costs. My regime-switching instinct (detect trend vs MR from auction balance) is not supported by these detectors.

title: H-AU1 design leaked look-ahead via 'one event per side per day'
body: Keeping one acceptance event per side per day favours days where price didn't come back (later re-crossings are dropped), so even a random walk through the same levels shows +0.09 sigma continuation. Caught by the agent with a simulated null before the holdout was computed. Rule (added to my checklist): every event study gets a simulated null through the SAME event-selection code, not only an analytic null.

title: Weekend options: the vol fact is true, the trade isn't there
body: Deribit daily ATM straddle sold Fri 08:00 -> Mon 08:00 UTC, hourly delta-hedged, real half-spreads + fees + hedge costs (Monday dailies only exist in Friday files since 2025-08-22: 45 IS + 15 holdout weekends per underlying). H-OPT1 net per weekend: BTC -0.17% (t -1.6), ETH -0.27% of notional; holdout also negative. H-OPT2 (weekend beats weekday control): no. H-OPT3 tail-sized annual return: -4.6% / -3.6%. Why my H-W7 inference was wrong: H-W7 compared weekend RV with the 7d ATM IV pro-rated by calendar time, but the TRADEABLE 3-day Friday option already prices the weekend ~20% cheaper than Monday's, and its window includes the Friday US session (realises 2-2.8x its implied share) and the Sunday reopen (1.1-1.7x). Hedging costs (~0.26% of notional) exceed the gross edge (0.09-0.25%). Lesson: an effect measured against a proxy (7d IV) is not an edge until it's measured against the price of the instrument you'd actually trade. Bybit dailies are listed 3 days ahead with 1-tick spreads, so a Fri 21:00 UTC entry with band hedging (H-OPT4) is the one variant left, forward-only, which needs a Bybit option-quote collector.

title: Regime switch (trend vs MR) can't be predicted out of sample
body: Walk-forward logistic on ER, directional-vol ratio, trend t-stats, VR, autocorrelation, vol percentile and vol-of-vol (61 monthly refits) predicting next-7d sign of (trend ensemble - MR ensemble): OOS IC -0.02 in-sample, +0.03 holdout; gating doesn't help; coefficients flip sign year to year (only the vol percentile is weakly stable: trend loses more in high vol). Single-feature ER14 terciles: wrong sign in-sample (efficient 2-week moves are followed by WORSE trend weeks, t -2.3). Placebo confirms no leakage. Third independent failure of the regime-switch idea (after VR and auction balance). Design note on me: a p > 0.5 gate against a 37% base rate is almost always off; but IC ~0 makes the threshold irrelevant. Belief update: in crypto at 4h, 'is it trending?' isn't forecastable from these state measures; regime context is descriptive, not a switch. Today all coins read P(trend wins) 0.27-0.34: choppy.

title: A6 trend-state-space: start H-BO1, H-MC1, H-KF1, H-KF2
body:
Agent A6 starts the trend/breakout/state-space block of the 2026-11-10 program. Design fixed before any result is seen:
- H-BO1: floor pivots from the prior complete UTC day (24 x 1h bars, non-zero range); first 1h close beyond R1 (long) / S1 (short) per day; signed next-4h/12h log return net of 15 bps round trip, in units of sigma_next*sqrt(h). Placebo (one per real event): same symbol, same segment, same side, same distance k = |log(level/C_prev)| / sigma_0 measured in the 1h sigma known at the prior close, re-anchored on a randomly drawn other day (seeded; redrawn until that day crosses its placebo level, max 200 draws). Secondary diagnostic: mirrored level (same day, same k, opposite side). Pivot minus placebo by OLS on an indicator with SE clustered by event date. Universes L and T.
- H-MC1: LazyBear WaveTrend (9, 12, SMA 4), dots at +/-53, VuManChu money-flow proxy SMA(((C-O)/(H-L))*150, 60) - 2.5 (MF>0 for longs, <0 for shorts when the filter is on); 4 variants {1h, 4h} x {MF on, off}; enter at the signal close, exit at the next opposite cross or 12 bars; net trade return in risk units (/sigma_next at entry), 7.5 bps per side; NW t; random entries matched per symbol/segment in count, side and holding (1000 draws); deflated Sharpe over the 4 variants on the daily portfolio series.
- H-KF1: smooth local-linear-trend (level noise 0) on 4h log price, q = slope variance / measurement variance in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}; adaptive R_t = sigma_risk_next(t-1)^2 with Q = q * Rref_t (Rref = trailing 180d median of R, causal) vs constant R (ratio q fixed): identical steady-state gain whenever R_t = Rref_t. Signal tanh(slope / trailing-180d sd(slope)); evaluate.strategy_pnl; paired daily net diff, NW t.
- H-KF2: monthly per-symbol MLE of the full LLT (eps, eta, zeta) on the trailing 180 days of 4h log closes (concentrated diffuse likelihood), q_hat = var(zeta)/var(eta) per the registry; Spearman IC vs next-30-day ensemble P&L from data/priors/trend_zoo_daily_4h.parquet; NW t over months.
- Multiple testing: Holm across this block's primary tests per segment; a t > 2 claim needs Holm p < 0.05 too.

title: A4 flow-anomaly: start of H-OF1..H-OF5 tests
body:
Agent A4 (program 2026-11-10). Building src/ai_trader/features/flow_anomaly.py (1m rollup of flow_3s, causal trailing-24h robust z for signed taker imbalance notional, trade count, volume, spread, depth25, |1m mid return|; liquidation-cluster detector: 1m liq notional > trailing-24h 99th pct and >= 3 prints; robust Mahalanobis with Ledoit-Wolf-shrunk covariance in numpy) and src/ai_trader/research/flow_anomaly_study.py.
Data: flow_3s linear perps (104 symbols; 52 from 2026-11-07 17:46, 52 from 2026-11-08 21:09), liquidations from 2026-11-08 00:46. Fixed as_of = 2026-11-10 22:30:00 UTC (reproducible; collector flushes every 5 min). First 24h per symbol is warm-up (no trailing window) and is dropped. Spot streams excluded (perps only; liquidations are perp events).
All results are clean_holdout: a short first sample (~3 days, one market state). Tests applied literally as registered; Holm across the 5 OF hypotheses; 1h calendar-hour block bootstrap (B=2000) for ratios, AUCs and lifts; hour-clustered t for signed means.
Implementation choices fixed before looking at outcomes: z uses window t-1440..t-1 (current minute excluded), min 720 valid minutes; MAD=0 falls back to 1.2533*mean abs deviation; anomaly = |z|>4; forward returns from the mid at the anomaly minute close; sigma_h = sqrt(h * trailing-24h mean squared 1m mid return); H-OF4 target |r_15m| > 2 sigma_15m, Mahalanobis on z clipped to +-20, fit on the first half by calendar time; H-OF5 alts = crypto perps excluding BTC and XAUT (TradFi perps excluded).

title: H-IC1 feature list fixed before testing
body:
Fixed before any H-IC1/2/3 code was run (agent A7, program 2026-11-10). Universe L (23 crypto perps), one row per
symbol and UTC day D; decision at the close of the last 1h bar of D (00:00 UTC D+1, repo convention: executed at that
close). Every input has event_ts < D+1 00:00; funding / OI prints count only if known_ts <= D+1 00:00:00.
sigma_d = sigma_risk_next (1h frame, robust_bc H-V1b) at the 23:00 bar of D x sqrt(24). Daily measures from
features.realized.daily_measures (1h bars, complete days only). Target y = 1{ret(D+1) > 0}, ret(D+1) = log close
00:00 D+2 / 00:00 D+1 (sign of the vol-scaled next-24h return).

The 32 features, ordered simple -> complex (model k uses features 1..k):
 1 ret_1d_z      ret_D / sigma_d
 2 ret_3d_z      sum ret D-2..D / (sigma_d sqrt 3)
 3 ret_7d_z      sum ret D-6..D / (sigma_d sqrt 7)
 4 ret_30d_z     sum ret D-29..D / (sigma_d sqrt 30)
 5 log_sigma     log sigma_d
 6 rv_surprise   log(RV_D / mean RV D-29..D)
 7 rv_term       log(mean RV 7d / mean RV 30d)
 8 vol_pct_1y    regime_features (4h)
 9 semivar_7d    log(sum RS- / sum RS+) over 7d (1h)
10 jump_share_7d sum JV / sum RV over 7d
11 vol_of_vol_30d regime_features
12 er_7d  13 er_30d  14 tstat_7d  15 tstat_30d  16 dvr_7d  17 dvr_30d  18 vr_30d  19 ac1_4h_30d  20 ac1_1d_30d
                 (features.regime_features on 4h bars, known at 00:00 D+1)
21 funding_1d    mean funding rate (bps) of prints known in (D 00:00, D+1 00:00], else last known
22 funding_z_90d (funding_1d - mean 90d) / sd 90d (>= 60 valid days)
23 oi_chg_1d     log OI(last known <= T) / OI(last known <= T-24h), Bybit 4h OI
24 oi_chg_7d     same over 7 days
25 next_is_weekend  1{D+1 is Sat/Sun}
26 next_is_monday   1{D+1 is Monday}
27 range_pos_30d (close_D - min low 30d) / (max high 30d - min low 30d) - 0.5
28 dd_90d_z      log(close_D / max close 90d) / (sigma_d sqrt 90)
29 day_range_z   log(high_D / low_D) / sigma_d
30 btc_ret_1d_z  BTCUSDT's ret_1d_z on D (market factor)
31 ret_7d_z x (vol_pct_1y - 0.5)
32 ret_1d_z x funding_z_90d

Fixed design choices (the registry leaves them open):
- Sample = rows with all 32 features and the target finite (identical rows for every k and window).
- Monthly walk-forward; training rows need label_end = T + 24h <= test_start - 1 day (purge 24h + embargo 1d);
  first test month = first with >= 365 distinct training dates; ridge logistic (Newton, lambda = 1 on standardised
  coefficients, intercept free; training mean/sd standardisation), regime_switch_study.fit_logit.
- Brier skill = 1 - Brier / Brier(training base rate of that refit), pooled per segment; 95% CI by moving-block
  bootstrap over decision dates, blocks of 10 days, 1000 draws, seed 0.
- Segments by decision: llm_in_sample if D+2 <= 2026-07-01, clean_holdout if D+1 >= 2026-07-01.
- H-IC1 per segment: inconclusive if every k's 95% CI contains 0; else supports iff argmax k <= 8 and
  skill(32) - max_{k<=8} skill <= 0, contradicts otherwise. pooled = supports iff both segments support;
  contradicts if any segment contradicts; else inconclusive. p (Holm) = bootstrap P*(Delta >= 0).
- H-IC2: k = in-sample argmax from H-IC1; windows 90/180/365/730 days of label ends + expanding; panel HAR = pooled
  log-HAR (1, log RV_D, log mean RV 5d, log mean RV 22d; common intercept), forecast exp(xb + s2/2), QLIKE on RV_{D+1};
  same monthly purged refits; rows common to all windows. Paired diff per date (mean over symbols, window - expanding),
  NW t over dates. Leg supports in a segment iff some shorter window has mean diff < 0 with t < -2 AND the mean loss is
  not strictly monotone in window length; leg contradicts if strictly monotone; else inconclusive. Segment verdict:
  supports iff both legs support, contradicts if any leg contradicts, else inconclusive. pooled = registry criterion
  (for each model a t < -2 win in at least one segment and no monotone segment). p = max over models of
  min_w Phi(t_w) x 4.
- H-IC3: shock_regime (as configured) on 1h bars; 4h trend-zoo ensemble computed on 4h bars and applied to 1h bars:
  the position held over the 1h bar after close c is the latest signal whose availability time (source bar close)
  is <= c - d hours (backward as-of). d in {0,1,2,4,8}; strategy_pnl conventions (risk units, 7.5 bps per side),
  daily net P&L by UTC date of event_ts; edge(d) = mean over dates of the cross-symbol mean daily P&L.
  Ratio R(d) = edge(d)/edge(0); test statistic g(d) = edge(d) - 0.5 edge(0) with 10-day block bootstrap CI (equivalent
  to the ratio CI excluding 0.5 when edge(0) > 0). Half-life = linear interpolation of the first crossing of 0.5.
  Trend leg: undefined (inconclusive) if edge(0) <= 0; supports iff R(4) > 0.5 and g(4) CI lower > 0; contradicts if
  R(4) < 0.5; else inconclusive. Shock leg: supports iff R(2) < 0.5 and g(2) CI upper < 0; contradicts if R(2) > 0.5.
  Segment: contradicts if a leg contradicts, supports if both support, else inconclusive. pooled = the llm_in_sample
  verdict (the registry criterion). p = max(P*(g4 <= 0), P*(g2 >= 0)).
- Holm over H-IC1..3 within each segment; a 'supports' whose Holm-adjusted p > 0.05 is downgraded to inconclusive.

title: A1 leverage block H-LEV1..5: design fixed before results
body:
Agent A1 (program 2026-11-10) starts testing H-LEV1..H-LEV5. Design fixed now, before any coefficient is seen (module src/ai_trader/research/leverage_study.py):
- Data: daily RV/RS-/RS+ from 1h bars via ai_trader.features.realized.daily_measures (complete UTC days). Universe L = 23 trend-zoo crypto perps. Universe T = Bybit TradFi perps with >= 120 complete days (15 of 16 candidates; SPCXUSDT has 117 and is excluded); H-LEV1 equity subset = TSLA INTC GOOGL AAPL MSTR NVDA MU QQQ SOXL (SPCX excluded). alt_series holds no equity index series (only alternative_me, defillama, deribit, deribit_svi), so the long-history index robustness is not available.
- Regressors need full consecutive-day windows (calendar reindexed, no row-based rolling over gaps). Origin = end of day t (known_ts); segment by origin vs 2026-07-01; 1-day targets never straddle the cutoff.
- Primary SHAR: levels, each symbol's RV-type variables divided by its mean RV in the estimation sample (equal weight per symbol), symbol fixed effects by demeaning, CR1 SE clustered by date. Robustness: log SHAR (semivariances floored at 1% of RV, as H-VCL2), Driscoll-Kraay SE, target-weekday calendar dummies, 4h SHAR for H-LEV2.
- GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t and EGARCH(1,1)-t (arch 8.0, constant mean, returns in percent, robust SE) per asset per segment with >= 250 days; otherwise n/a (full-sample fits for shorter series are exploratory only).
- H-LEV3 drawdown flag: ln(close_t / max daily close t-29..t) < -1.5 * std(daily ret t-29..t) * sqrt(30); primary = SHAR + RS-xD + RS+xD (as registered), robustness adds D.
- H-LEV4: pooled panel log-HAR vs log-SHAR with FE, lognormal bias correction, expanding window refit every 30 days; levels as robustness; paired QLIKE averaged by date, NW t.
- H-LEV5: levels HAR + RS- + fz + RS-xfz, fz = (latest funding known at origin - mean)/std over funding prints in the trailing 90 days (>= 90 prints), clipped to +-5.
- Verdicts: registered criteria literally; Holm within the LEV block per segment, raw and adjusted reported. In-sample recorded before the holdout is computed.

title: A3 vol-signals: H-VB1..H-VB4 design fixed before results
body:
Agent A3 (program 2026-11-10) starts H-VB1..H-VB4. Module: src/ai_trader/research/vol_signal_study.py. Design fixed BEFORE any result is seen:

Data: market_frame 1h and 4h per symbol (funding/oi off); daily measures via features.realized.daily_measures on the same 1h bars (identical to daily_panel). Universe L = trend_zoo_study.UNIVERSE (23), T = the 16 TradFi perps. Segment = decision timestamp (known_ts of the forecast-origin day, or close of the entry bar) vs knowledge_cutoff 2026-07-01.

Daily variance forecast: L per-symbol har_forecast_x (log-HAR, min_days 180, refit 30d). T has 115-555 days only, so T uses a pooled log-HAR (common slopes, expanding window, refit every 30 days, first fit after 300 pooled pairs) with two calendar regressors known at t (target day is Sat/Sun; target day is Monday) because TradFi perps have ~5x lower weekend RV.

H-VB1 primary (verdict): factor level as in Moreira-Muir: EW long-only portfolio of the universe and EW trend-zoo ensemble (4h, recomputed with the same zoo/strategy_pnl execution policy, checked against data/priors/trend_zoo_daily_4h.parquet), weight w_D = c / sigma2_hat_D with sigma2_hat = HAR forecast of the EW index's daily RV (index built from EW 1h simple returns, RV from daily_measures), c = full-sample vol match (alpha t is invariant to a constant c). Variants reported, not used for the verdict: real-time c (expanding), MM-native sigma2 = sum of the previous 22 daily squared base returns, per-symbol HAR scaling then EW. Cost 7.5 bps per side on |delta weight| (managed long-only) and on |delta (w*leverage)| per 4h bar (managed ensemble). Spanning regression alpha, HAC t (NW auto lag). DSR over the 16 variant series.

H-VB2: event day t: RV_t > 1.5 F_t and |ret_t| > sqrt(F_t) (F_t = forecast made at end of t-1); decluster 3 days per symbol; signed next-1d / 3d returns / sqrt(h F_{t+1|t}), net of 2 x 7.5 bps; t from NW on the date-mean series; pooled L+T; split by v0 vol state at the START of day t (1h regimes.label at the last bar of t-1: the state the surprise arrived into), also reported at end of t. Baseline: all non-event days signed by their own return.

H-VB3 (4h): BB(20,2) with population sd, KC = EMA20 +- 1.5 x SMA20(TR); squeeze = BB inside KC; release = first non-squeeze bar after >= 6 squeeze bars; event = first close outside BB at or after release, before the next squeeze starts and within 20 bars. Non-squeeze BB breakouts = fresh closes outside BB (previous close inside) with no >= 6-bar squeeze ended in the last 20 bars. Decluster 6 bars per symbol and class. Signed log(c_{t+6}/c_t) / (sigma_next_t sqrt 6) net of 2 x 7.5 bps. Mean t: NW on date means; difference: OLS dummy with SE clustered by date. Random-entry baseline: 200 draws of random bars per symbol matched in count, sign = side of close vs BB mid.

H-VB4 (1h): exceedance = |ret_t| > 2 sigma_t, sigma_t = sigma_risk_next of bar t-1 (robust EWMA, known at t-1). Per symbol Hawkes (exp kernel, the fit_hawkes continuous-time likelihood, evaluated with a vectorised bar-grid filter, equality tested against jump_diffusion._hawkes_nll), expanding window, refit monthly; intensity via hawkes_intensity; next-24h expectation iterates E[A] through the 24 bars (exact for the discrete linear filter). Baseline: per-bar variance F_{D+1}/24 (flat intraday), unit-variance Student-t with df fitted by MLE on L llm_in_sample hourly returns standardised by sqrt(F/24); p = P(|r| > 2 sigma_0), sigma_0 = threshold sigma at the decision bar, rate 24p. Score: Poisson log pmf of the next-day count; paired diff averaged per date, NW t. Constant-rate Poisson reported as reference.

Verdicts: success criteria literally; supports additionally needs Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 across the 4 VB primaries in that segment. Holdout rows: criterion as registered (VB1-3 same sign; VB4 t > 2); pooled row = overall verdict.

title: A2 vol tournament: start (H-VM1..H-VM5)
body:
Agent A2 starts the volatility-model tournament of program 2026-11-10.
Plan, fixed before looking at results: daily RV from 1h bars via features.realized (complete UTC days, known at day end);
targets RV_{t+1} and mean RV_{t+1..t+5}; universe L = 23 crypto perps (trend_zoo UNIVERSE), universe T = TradFi perps with >= 120 complete days.
Contestants: EWMA(0.94) daily, robust_bc (24 x sigma_risk_next^2 at the day's last 1h bar, risk version; plus the tool's weekend-aware central aggregation),
GARCH(1,1)-t, GJR-t, EGARCH-t (arch 8.0, monthly refit, analytic 5d for GARCH/GJR, Monte Carlo 5d for EGARCH),
level HAR / HAR-Q / SHAR / HAR-J / range-HAR (GK, PK, RV+GK), log-HAR (lognormal back-transform), panel versions (pooled slopes,
symbol fixed effects; level panels scale-normalised by the symbol training mean so slopes pool across vol levels), factor panel log-HAR
(cross-sectional mean log RV of L), SV state-space (log r^2 = h + log chi2 noise, QML Kalman; plus calibrated and log-RV-measurement variants as flagged extensions).
Expanding window, refit every 30 days, per-asset min 180 days; panel fit on L u T, a symbol enters once it has 30 training pairs.
Loss QLIKE + MSE(log); paired date-averaged differences vs per-asset HAR (levels, Corsi) with NW t; MCS Tmax, block 10, B=1000, 90%; Holm within VM.
Verdict rule per segment: supports if the registered criterion holds; contradicts if the point estimate has the wrong sign; inconclusive otherwise.

title: A4 flow-anomaly: data gaps, late candles and a degenerate spread z found in a 6-symbol debug run
body:
A mechanics check on 6 symbols (BTC, ETH, SOL, DOGE, NVDA, ASTER; as_of 2026-11-10 22:30 UTC) showed outcome numbers for those symbols before the full run; I'm recording that openly. No threshold, horizon or test was changed because of those outcomes. What it exposed:
1) flow_3s has collector-wide outages: about 37% of minutes are missing for BTC (UTC, approx.: 11-08 14:00-15:00 and 17:00-19:00; 11-09 08:20-13:00, 17:00-22:00 and 23:00 to 11-10 12:00 (about 13h); 11-10 17:15-19:30). With the start-entry rule (>= 720 valid minutes in the trailing 24h), the CPI afternoon of 11-10 got no scores. Decision: min_valid = 360 (6h). The window is still the trailing 24h of clock time. Liquidations during outage minutes are set to unknown, not zero.
2) Point in time: some 3 s candles have known_ts up to ~10h after event_ts (finalised after a reconnect). Rolling them into minute t would use information that wasn't available at t+1m, so candles finalised > 60 s after their end are dropped.
3) Spread z is degenerate on 1-tick books. The TWA spread in bps moves only with the price level, MAD is ~1e-6 bps, and |z| > 4 showed up in 46% of minutes. Fix: scale floored at 1% of |median| for every feature (no effect when the median is ~0, e.g. imbalance and liquidations).
Because 3) changes an H-OF4 competitor after the debug output (spread was the best single feature there), H-OF4 counts as supported only if it also holds under the original spec (min_valid 720, no floor), which is run as a sensitivity. The 1/2 lag fixes are kept in both runs.
Observation: on the registered definition, |z_imbalance| > 4 is not rare (about 28% of scored minutes in the debug sample). Signed 1m taker imbalance is extremely heavy-tailed relative to its 24h MAD.

title: H-IC1..3 decision-budget study started
body:
Running src/ai_trader/research/decision_budget_study.py (design and the 32-feature list exactly as fixed in the entry

title: A6: first run silently dropped 10 of 16 TradFi perps (no native 4h history)
body: The first full run of breakout_cipher_kalman_study skipped TSLA INTC GOOGL AAPL MSTR NVDA MU QQQ SOXL SPCX as "no data": the lake has their 1h bars from late Apr/May 2026 but native 4h bars only from 2026-11-04, so the 4h market_frame was empty after the 30-day listing burn-in and the job skipped the whole symbol (including the 1h pivot study). Nothing was recorded from that run. Fix: when native 4h history is < 80% of the 1h history, build 4h bars from complete UTC-aligned groups of four 1h bars (known_ts = max of the four; same sanity filter, burn-in, enrich_bars, add_robust_vol); validated on BTC against native 4h (identical highs, sigma diff < 3e-4). Re-running before any recording. Lesson: a per-symbol skip must be reported per data need, not per symbol.

title: A6: rolling LLT MLE puts the slope variance at zero most months
body: In the first (unrecorded) run, 65% of the 1272 monthly 180-day LLT fits on 4h crypto log prices put q_hat = var(zeta)/var(eta) at the lower bound (exp(-16)); the 90th percentile is ~2e-5. This is the known pile-up of the MLE of a small state variance at zero (Shephard & Harvey 1990): at 4h, a 180-day window cannot distinguish a stochastic slope from a random walk. So H-KF2's q_hat is mostly a tie at zero, and the IC uses tie-averaged ranks.

title: A1 leverage: H-LEV2 verdict mapping had an extra gamma conjunct
body: While dry-running the in-sample segment (not yet recorded) I found my verdict code for H-LEV2 required median GJR gamma <= 0 in addition to the registered success criterion (difference t < 2 supports no leverage). The registered criterion is the decider, so the mapping now follows it literally; median gamma (in-sample 0.004 across 23 crypto perps, 0/23 with t > 2, 2/23 with t < -2) is reported next to the verdict. No test design, data or estimator changed. Disclosed because the change moves the in-sample label from inconclusive to supports.

title: Decision budget H-IC1..3: more inputs hurt, 1-2y history suffices, trend tolerates hours of latency
body:
H-IC1 (sign of next-24h return, 23 crypto, monthly purged ridge-logit): OOS Brier skill k=1 +0.0004 [-0.004,+0.005], k=8 -0.003,
k=16 -0.007 [CI<0], k=32 -0.015 [-0.023,-0.007] llm_in_sample (34,434 rows, 1,703 dates) -> supports by the literal rule (argmax k=1,
Delta(32 vs <=8) -0.015, Holm p 0.003), but no k has skill > 0: more features only add noise. clean_holdout (3,036 rows, 132 dates):
best k=8 +0.007 [-0.001,+0.014], all CIs contain 0 -> inconclusive. pooled inconclusive.
H-IC2 (k=1 logit + pooled log-HAR, windows 90/180/365/730/expanding): no shorter window beats expanding with t<-2 anywhere; 90d HAR is
worse (QLIKE +0.013, t +3.1 IS); best IS 365d logit (t -1.7), 730d HAR (t -0.4); holdout best = expanding for both -> inconclusive
all segments. More history never hurt; gains flatten after 1-2 years.
H-IC3 (lag d=0..8h, 1h bars): 4h trend ensemble IS edge 0.112/day (t 2.4), R(4h) 0.97 [0.79,1.09], R(8h) 0.88, half-life >8h -> trend
leg holds. shock_regime IS edge(0) 0.010 (t 1.05), R(1h) 0.61, R(2h) 0.10, half-life ~1.2h, but CI of g(2) includes 0 -> leg
inconclusive; verdict inconclusive. Holdout edge(0) < 0 for both -> ratios undefined, inconclusive. All rows recorded (9 rows).
Surprise: the size of the large-k penalty (16 and 32 features significantly worse than the base rate in-sample).
Implication for the LLM layer (rule candidates R-IC-1..4 in the report): short card, long-window parameters, slow signals can wait,
shock signals execute mechanically with LLM veto only. H-IC4 remains the forward test of whether this transfers to the LLM.

title: A2 vol tournament: two estimator fixes found in the one-symbol smoke test (before any evaluation)
body:
Smoke test on PAXGUSDT alone (no pooled evaluation run yet):
1) EGARCH-t refits landed on degenerate optima (alpha ~ 367, beta = 1, nu ~ 2.07) at some refit dates, both warm- and cold-started -> next-day QLIKE ~1e16.
   Fix (generic, not tuned): each refit fits warm-started and cold-started, keeps the higher-loglik fit among sane ones (GARCH/GJR stationary; EGARCH |beta| < 1,
   |alpha|, |gamma| < 2; nu > 2.05), else keeps the previous parameters.
2) Level HAR-Q forecasts collapsed onto the clip floor (the training-minimum RV, a quiet weekend day), QLIKE 6.9. The clip-to-range insanity filter was replaced by the
   Bollerslev-Patton-Quaedvlieg (2016) rule (an out-of-range forecast becomes the training mean), for every level model, per-asset and panel.
Both changes are literature-standard and were fixed before looking at any pooled or holdout result.

title: A3: event-study estimate and its t used different weightings (fixed before recording)
body: First full run of vol_signal_study: primaries() took the plain event mean as the estimate while the t-stat came from NW on the date-mean series (the declared method). For H-VB3 llm_in_sample these disagree in sign (event mean +0.009 sigma, date mean -0.079 sigma, t -2.07): days with many simultaneous crypto breakouts carry outsized weight in the event mean. Fixed: the primary estimate is now the mean of per-date means (consistent with its t); the event mean is reported alongside. No verdict had been recorded. Also checked: the recomputed 4h trend-zoo ensemble equals data/priors/trend_zoo_daily_4h.parquet on every symbol-day except each symbol's first evaluation day (<= 0.031 risk units) and the parquet's partial last day (2026-11-07).

title: A1 leverage block: no leverage effect in crypto or TradFi perps; SHAR adds nothing; funding x down-day interaction negative
body:
H-LEV1..H-LEV5 recorded (15 rows: llm_in_sample, clean_holdout, pooled). The in-sample rows were recorded before the holdout was computed.
- H-LEV1 (TradFi equity leverage): inconclusive in-sample (only 18 dates) / contradicts in the holdout. Level SHAR b(RS-) 0.23 vs b(RS+) 0.51, diff t -2.11 over 132 dates and 9 perps. The result is fragile: log t +0.22, weekday-dummies t -1.79. GJR is n/a (< 250 days); exploratory GJR gammas are 8/9 positive, none significant. The lake has no equity index series.
- H-LEV2 (no crypto leverage): supports in all segments. In-sample diff -0.03 (t -0.28, 2252 dates), holdout -0.20 (t -1.57), 4h t -0.04. Median GJR gamma 0.004 (0/23 with t > 2). This confirms V8 / H-VCL2 with panel power.
- H-LEV3 (drawdown asymmetry): inconclusive / contradicts. Crypto RS- x D +0.10 (t 0.59); TradFi holdout -0.17 (t -2.20).
- H-LEV4 (SHAR beats HAR for TradFi only): inconclusive / contradicts. Log form: SHAR is worse (L +0.0025 t 1.95 in-sample, T +0.0056 t 2.22 in the holdout). Levels: crypto SHAR is marginally better (-0.0017, t -2.27), which is negligible.
- H-LEV5 (RS- x funding z): contradicts in-sample, with the interaction negative (-0.050, t -2.30); holdout -0.10 (t -1.23). Funding z on its own raises next-day RV (+0.07 x mean RV per z unit, t 2.36 in-sample; t 2.71 in the holdout). This is exploratory and should be registered as its own hypothesis.
- Holm within the block: no positive-direction test survives in any segment.
Decision implication: keep the vol model symmetric (plain log HAR) for both asset classes; there is no leverage or drawdown uplift. Five rule candidates (R-VOL-LEV-1..5) are in the report.

title: Register a funding-z main-effect vol hypothesis?
body: H-LEV5 found, as a by-product, that crypto funding z (vs trailing 90d) on its own predicts higher next-day RV: +0.07 x mean RV per z unit, t 2.36 in-sample and t 2.71 in the holdout. It was not the registered test. Should the orchestrator or user register it (e.g. H-LEV6: HAR + funding_z, OOS QLIKE) before anyone uses it?

title: A6 results: pivots and Cipher dots carry no edge; adaptive Kalman gain marginal; LLT q_hat useless
body:
Recorded 8 rows (H-BO1, H-MC1, H-KF1, H-KF2 x llm_in_sample / clean_holdout). Universe L 23 crypto, T 15 TradFi (SPCX < 120 days). Holm across 12 primary tests per segment.
- H-BO1 (null) supports / supports: pivot minus same-sigma-distance placebo +0.005 sigma (t 0.48) at 4h and +0.015 (t 1.51) at 12h in-sample (L, 26k events); holdout L -0.046 (t -1.27) / -0.060 (t -1.78), T +0.036 (0.60) / +0.074 (1.44). Breakouts have ~0 gross continuation (+0.02 sigma at 4h), net -0.09 sigma (t -5.1). The mirrored same-day placebo gives a large spurious difference (t 5-21) because it only exists on wide two-sided days: a selection artefact, noted.
- H-MC1 (null) supports / supports: DSR 0.00 for all 4 variants in-sample (SR0 1.6/yr); best in-sample variant 4h+MF (+0.038 per trade, t 0.34, beat random p 0.022) lost -0.60 per trade in the holdout (t -2.8, worse than random 97% of the time). 1h unfiltered -0.30 (t -9.7) in-sample, -0.44 (t -4.9) holdout.
- H-KF1 contradicts / supports(sign): adaptive minus constant at q=1e-3 +0.0106/day (t 1.49, Holm p 0.92) in-sample, +0.0218 (t 1.26) holdout; positive in 5 of 6 q x segment cells, signal correlation 0.96. Not supported overall.
- H-KF2 contradicts / contradicts: mean IC -0.023 (t -0.63, 55 months), holdout -0.15 (4 months); q_hat at its zero bound in 65% of fits.
Rule candidates R-TS-1..4 in the report (all "don't use X for Y" except a C-grade tie-breaker preference for the adaptive gain).

title: A3 vol-signals: H-VB1..H-VB4 all fail (four do-not-expect rules)
body:
Recorded (12 rows). Segment = decision timestamp vs 2026-07-01; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0 for every primary except VB2 holdout (0.51).
H-VB1 variance-managed exposure (factor level, w = c / HAR forecast of EW-index RV, 7.5 bps on weight changes): L in-sample spanning alpha long-only -0.23/yr (t -1.24), trend ensemble +4.5 risk units/yr (t 1.00); holdout L -0.28 (t -0.56) / +1.05 (t 0.14); T holdout -0.11 (t -0.25) / -15.9 (t -0.49). Inconclusive in all segments. Best variant (MM 22d RV on the ensemble) t 2.08 in-sample, holdout t 0.16, DSR 0.005 over 10 trials.
H-VB2 daily vol surprise (RV > 1.5 F, |ret| > 1 sigma_f): signed 3d net -0.008 sigma (t -0.25, 2620 events / 763 dates) in-sample -> contradicts; holdout +0.150 (t 1.14, 345 events) = sign only; T holdout +0.37 (t 2.1). Low-vol-state subset in-sample +0.064 (t 1.2), high -0.059 (t -1.2): P1 ordering, not significant.
H-VB3 4h squeeze-release breakouts: in-sample net -0.079 sigma (t -2.07, 2262 events), plain BB breakouts -0.068 (t -2.90), diff +0.02 (t 0.48) -> contradicts; holdout squeeze +0.02 (t 0.17), diff +0.30 (t 1.82). Breakouts lose net of costs in crypto at 4h.
H-VB4 Hawkes on 1h 2-sigma exceedances vs HAR+Student-t (nu 3.35): log-score diff -0.014 nats/symbol-day (t -2.14) in-sample, -0.019 (t -0.70) holdout -> contradicts both. Exceedances scaled by the robust sigma barely self-excite (branching 0.05, half-life 2.1 h); HAR-t carries the information (corr with counts 0.31 vs 0.03) but over-predicts counts by 11-16%.
Surprise: the Hawkes adds nothing once sigma is robust-EWMA; the useful signal is the daily HAR forecast relative to the current hourly sigma.

title: A2 vol tournament: EGARCH variance-path collapse found in the first evaluation pass (nothing recorded yet)
body:
The first evaluation pass (not recorded) showed EGARCH-t forecasts at ~1e-21 x realised for whole 30-day refit blocks (DOGE 2022, UNI, ETC, ENA, XAUT):
optima that passed the parameter checks but drive ln sigma^2 to the -50 floor. In-sample QLIKE ratio vs HAR ~1e17, which also makes EGARCH a meaningless MCS member.
Fix: a refit is accepted only if its in-sample filtered variance stays within [1e-3, 1e3] x the sample variance (applied to GARCH, GJR and EGARCH alike);
otherwise the next candidate (warm/cold start) or the previous parameters are used. The full build is rerun; no other estimator or evaluation choice is changed.
First-pass impressions for transparency (not results of record): log-HAR leads in-sample; GK-input HAR loses to RV-input HAR; holdout MCS keeps most models.

title: A2 vol tournament: H-VM1..H-VM5 results and the recommended daily risk model
body:
25 contestants, 38 symbols (L 23 crypto, T 15 TradFi; SPCX excluded at 116 days), date-averaged QLIKE, NW t, MCS Tmax 90% (block 10, B 1000).
H-VM1 panel HAR vs per-asset HAR (levels, pooled L u T): in-sample supports (h1 -1.6% t -3.42; h5 -3.0% t -3.09; Holm p 0.003); holdout inconclusive (-0.7% t -0.85; -1.2% t -1.11).
  Gain is in 1-2y-history assets; log panel ~= per-asset log-HAR. For <180d history the panel is the only HAR: p_loghar -27.5% vs robust_bc x24 holdout (t -5.2).
H-VM2: in-sample supports (HAR-Q -5.1% t -6.8, log-HAR -11.9% t -5.0, panels likewise); holdout inconclusive: HAR-Q passes (t -3.3 / panel -4.1) but log-HAR -4.7% has t -0.42.
H-VM3 contradicts both segments: GK-HAR +5.4% (t 4.9) / +15.7% (t 4.8) QLIKE vs RV-HAR; RV+GK no better than RV.
H-VM4 inconclusive both: factor R^2 median 0.72 / 0.68 passes, forecast gain -0.1% (t -0.6) / -1.0% (t -1.6) fails.
H-VM5 supports (weak): L 1d winner loghar in holdout MCS (p 0.17, rank 6), 5d winner p_loghar in (p 0.29, rank 14); but holdout MCS keeps 22/25 and 25/25 models.
Recommended default (rule fixed in code before evaluation): crypto 1d per-asset log-HAR (= vol.har; -17.6% QLIKE vs robust_bc x24 in-sample, -18% holdout);
crypto 5d direct panel log-HAR; TradFi 1d panel HAR-Q, 5d level panel HAR (both holdout-selected, confidence C). robust_bc scaled to days is near-worst everywhere: keep it per-bar only.
Descriptive: every model over-forecasts Saturdays (crypto Sat RV 0.5x Tue-Fri, log bias +0.9; TradFi 0.05-0.1x, bias +2.7..+3.7); proposed follow-up H-VM6 weekday-aware HAR (not registered).
