title: Research program: participants ML, intraday + geometry, stress tests (3 agents)
body:
User 2026-11-25 ~22:15 UTC: identify research gaps; ML on market participants; intraday structure across days; market geometry for executable edge; stress test every strategy in every scenario; up to 3 agents.
Gap analysis (registry: 285 hypotheses, 224 with results): participant/flow families mostly untested (flow 4 untested, adverse_selection 2, tape_footprints 1, cross_venue_flow 2, xvenue_arb 2; atx tape labels never validated as predictive); intraday structure across days for alts not studied (calendar 4 supports / 6 inconclusive; microstructure_dist 13 contradicts); geometry mixed (levels 4 contradicts / 1 supports, bos_regime 3/1, auction 2/2, trend_breakout 2 supports) and never translated into executable rules after realistic fills; no unified stress harness across strategies and scenarios (regimes, crises, costs, latency, parameters, synthetic paths, correlation, liquidity, risk-engine limits).
Agents: PART (participant taxonomy + predictive value beyond OFI + executable translation + a PIT feature set), GEO (intraday map, geometry event studies, executable rules after costs), STRESS (scorecard of every deterministic strategy x scenario with pre-registered SURVIVES/FRAGILE/FAILS rules; the LLM layer is never backtested). Each registers hypotheses before fitting and records every result.

title: GEO design frozen before results
body: Agent GEO (intraday structure and market geometry, user request 2026-11-25 ~22:15 UTC). Registered H-GEO1..H-GEO17 (research/hypotheses.yaml, block GEO) and froze the design in data/research/intraday_geometry/design.json before computing any outcome. Data: Bybit 5m klines for universe L (23 perps) 2022-01..2026-11-25 (BOS cache + public REST extension), funding, flow_3s (spread/depth 2026-11-07 on), liquidations (2026-11-08 on), CPI/NFP/FOMC times. Task 1 (intraday map): H-GEO1 vol/volume hour-of-week stability, H-GEO2 direction map (expected noise), H-GEO3 release minutes, H-GEO4/5 funding settlement vol and direction, H-GEO6 session-open vol step and DST, H-GEO7 month-end, H-GEO8 spread/depth profile (holdout only). Task 2 (geometry): 13 objects x 4 events (touch, sweep-reclaim, accept, retest) x 3 horizons vs placebo levels, BH 10% in-sample, survivors read once in holdout (H-GEO9); named classic cells H-GEO10..14; regime/session heterogeneity H-GEO15; liquidation clusters exploratory H-GEO17. Task 3: rules from survivors (or best-of-grid + named cells if none), 16 exit variants, purged expanding walk-forward, DSR/PBO, costs pegged 2.0+1.3 bp, taker 5.5+2.0 bp, latency 0/5 min, regime-matched random entries (H-GEO16). Prior expectation: vol patterns stable, direction patterns noise, intraday rules fail after costs (R-BOS-1).

title: PART design frozen before results
body:
Registered H-PART1..H-PART8 (research/hypotheses.yaml, block PART) before any fit and before reducing any data beyond a
speed test of the book reducer (one BTC day, timing only, no statistics looked at).

Data. BTCUSDT ETHUSDT SOLUSDT XRPUSDT DOGEUSDT linear perps. Days: the 12 pre-cutoff micro_days dates (2025-08-31, 09-02,
09-05, 09-10, 11-19, 11-21, 12-18, 2026-01-25, 05-11, 05-20, 06-14, 06-21; llm_in_sample) + every UTC day 2026-10-06 ..
2026-11-24 (50 days, clean_holdout) = 62 days. Raw = public.bybit.com prints + quote-saver ob200, downloaded to
data/raw/participants/<date>/, reduced, deleted. micro_days book_1s lacks add/cancel flows, so all 62 days are rebuilt
from raw with the same order definition (same-ms same-side print runs).

Split (fixed now). FIT = 12 pre-cutoff days + 2026-10-06 .. 10-29 (36 days); HELD = 2026-10-30 .. 11-24 (26 days), read once.
FIT CV = 6 chronological blocks of FIT days, 1-day embargo each side. Segments: llm_in_sample (pre-cutoff FIT days) vs
clean_holdout (post-cutoff FIT days, and all HELD).

Taxonomy. Unit = taker order. 11 trait features (lognot, rel_l1, rel_d10, ticks, nprints, dt_any, dt_same, n1s, n10s,
clip20, sigdig), robust-standardised per symbol on FIT, clipped +-6, pooled GMM full covariance; k in 2..10 by the rule
ARI >= 0.80 (10 bootstrap fits of 30k, common 20k eval set) then min BIC (100k sample). k-means at the chosen k as a
cross-check. Time of day, side, notional share and markouts are descriptors, not clustering features (so types are
behaviours, not clock hours). Book add/cancel/refill rates describe the MAKER side and go into the 1-minute flow-state
HMM (features h_lognot, h_imb, h_absr, h_ofi, h_upd, h_cxl, h_refill, h_spread; diagonal Gaussian, K in 2..6, same rule
on day-block bootstraps of FIT symbol-days), used only through its forward filter. Design choice stated: the public tape
only shows aggressors, so "participants" = taker types + maker-side book states.

Supervised. 1-minute grid per symbol, rows from 01:00 UTC, labels inside the day. Targets r1 r5 r60 (vol-standardised),
ln RV 5/60 min (10 s mid returns), AS10/AS60 (touch-maker markout of next-minute taker orders). Baselines and participant
sets exactly as in H-PART3/4/5. Pooled OLS with day-clustered SEs for inference; OOS dR2 for the criterion; day-block
bootstrap 2000 (seed 20261125); Holm within hypothesis. Logistic + Platt and LightGBM (depth <= 3) only as registered.
Executable (H-PART6): 5 fixed variants, latency >= 1 s (1 s book resolution), fees maker 2 / taker 5.5 / pegged 2.0 + 1.3 bp.
xvenue (H-PART7) only 2026-11-15 .. 11-24 (journal coverage), tape sanity (H-PART8) 2026-11-15 .. 11-24.

Not done: no liquidation flag exists in the public prints (lake liquidations only from 2026-11-08), so LIQ types are not a
clustering target; they are checked descriptively on HELD days. Cross-venue lead/lag per order is impossible (xvenue is a
~2-min snapshot), so it enters only as H-PART7.

title: GEO part 1: intraday map (H-GEO1..8)
body: Universe L 23 perps, 5m 2022-01..2026-11-25, pooled per timestamp. VOLATILITY (forecastable): hour-of-week variance shape in-sample vs holdout Spearman 0.77 (volume 0.81); 93%/96% of in-sample months have rho >= 0.5 with the leave-month-out profile, 80% of holdout months -> H-GEO1 supports in-sample, inconclusive holdout (0.77 < 0.8). Release minutes: first 5m after CPI/NFP/FOMC = 13.6x baseline in-sample [9.4, 18.8] (CPI 21.7x, FOMC 16.6x, NFP 4.8x), 16.5x holdout [4.6, 36.5] (n 13), decays to 2.9x / 1.7x by 30-60 min; pre-release 30 min already 1.4x / 1.3x -> H-GEO3 supports both. US cash open: 30 min after / before = 2.9x in-sample (mean of daily ratios; 1.9x ratio of means), holdout supports; off-clock check passes in EDT (1.08) but not EST (1.75, the 08:30 ET slot, other 08:30 ET releases not excluded) -> H-GEO6 inconclusive in-sample, supports holdout. Asia 00 UTC step 2.7x (confounded with funding + day roll), London 1.8x. Funding settlement 5m bars vs neighbouring top-of-hour bars: 1.20x in-sample (CI 0.99-1.51), 0.71x holdout -> H-GEO4 inconclusive / contradicts. Month-end 15-16 UTC: 0.77x in-sample, 0.42x holdout -> H-GEO7 contradicts. Spread profile (flow_3s, 18 days): spreads are widest in Asia hours (00-08 UTC) and tightest 09-15 UTC, i.e. they track participation, not variance (rho spread-var -0.01, depth-var -0.39) -> H-GEO8 contradicts as registered. DIRECTION (noise): hour-of-week mean z joint chi2 185.7 on 168 df p 0.17 in-sample, 8 cells |t|>2 (chance 7.6); in-sample vs holdout rank rho 0.03; tilt gross -0.025 R/h vs 0.21 R/h cost -> H-GEO2 contradicts. Funding drift into the print (signed by -sign prev funding): +0.018 z t 1.8 in-sample, +0.014 t 0.4 holdout -> H-GEO5 inconclusive both; holdout post-settlement -0.10 t -2.4 is a single-segment observation, not tested.

title: STRESS design frozen before results
body: User request 2026-11-25 ~22:15 UTC: stress test every strategy in every scenario. Design frozen and registered (block STRESS in research/hypotheses.yaml) before any stress number was computed; the only runs so far were a timing probe (signal compute time and signal-magnitude quantiles on BTCUSDT, no P&L). Units: 17 registered strategies + zoo_ensemble through one generic trade layer (enter |s| >= 0.3, exit on flat/flip, exchange stop 4 sigma_risk per bar = applied stop cap, R normalised to the at-risk sizing budget, live costs: pegged-limit entry 3.3 bp, taker exits 7.5 bp), plus desk setups trend_4h, shock_desk, hs2_fade_blackout (R-FLOW-2 = entry one 1h bar later), hrb2 (post_cascade_study logic), setup_c_proxy (setup C WITHOUT its spot-absorption and Coinbase-premium confirmations, which have no history: a proxy, said so in the report), weekend MM via its replay results only. Scenarios S0..S9 (slices, 10+ crisis windows, fees x1.5/x2, slip +5/+10/+25, gap / next-open stop fills, no stop, latency 1/5/15 min by Brownian-bridge fills, +-20/50% one-at-a-time + 30 joint parameter draws on D8, 1000 synthetic paths SBB + RS, co-stopping in down states, liquidity drought on mid/illiquid tiers, live_small engine with daily-stop / losing-run / time-under-water / 3-month loss probabilities). Verdict rules: FAILS if base or fees x1.5 mean net R <= 0; FRAGILE if a +-20% parameter cliff, 5-min latency sign flip, a crisis window < -20 R on the engine stream, +5 bp sign flip, holdout mean <= 0 (>= 20 trades), base CI includes 0, or the total without the top 5 trades <= 0; else SURVIVES. Choices I made that change strategies: the 0.3 entry threshold (cuts rsi_reversion to its extreme readings) and the 4-sigma per-bar exchange stop (the live engine's cap; it will stop out long-holding 1h trend trades often) - both are also perturbed in S5 and the no-stop variant is reported.

title: GEO implementation clarifications before the geometry inference
body: Written before stage infer (no real-vs-placebo statistic computed yet). (1) Approach side: the registered text says 'fixed by the close before the window'; implemented as the side on which price first stands >= 0.5 hourly sigma from the level, counting the close before the window first. This is identical to the registered rule whenever that close is already >= 0.5 sigma away and only differs for levels that start at the price (PD_C, VWAPs, OR edges right after the range), where the registered wording is degenerate. (2) Funding sign for H-GEO5 = previous settled rate (known 8 h before), stricter than 'known one hour before'. (3) US-open days exclude NYSE holidays (features.seasonality.NYSE_HOLIDAYS), stricter than the registered 'not modelled'. (4) Disclosure: a pipeline smoke test on BTCUSDT printed per-event mean y12 for real levels (both segments pooled, no placebo) before inference; nothing was changed after it and it is not used for any selection. (5) Session-open and release windows use the pooled 5m series; per-day ratios are reported as registered (mean of ratios) plus the ratio of means and the geometric mean.

title: GEO part 2: geometry event studies (H-GEO9..15)
body: 13 objects x 4 events x 3 horizons, first test per level window, 23 perps, real minus 2 placebo levels (+-0.5..1.5 daily sigma), day-clustered NW. 15 of 156 cells survive BH 10% in llm_in_sample; 4 of them pass the holdout BH (one-sided): PD_HL touch 15m +0.15 sigma vs placebo (in +0.18 t 7.0; holdout t 2.2), PW_HL touch 1h +0.26 (in +0.33 t 6.3; ho t 2.6), PW_HL touch 4h (+0.21 t 4.6 / ho t 2.0), PW_HL sweep 1h (+0.21 t 3.0 / ho t 2.0) -> H-GEO9 supports both segments. Every holdout-confirmed effect is CONTINUATION: the first touch of the prior day's / week's high or low breaks further than a placebo level does (consistent with R-PX-4), not a hold. p_cont stays below 0.5 (0.46-0.49): the mean is carried by the continuation tail, not the hit rate. Size in price: 0.1-0.18 sigma at 15m-1h is about 5-8 bp on a 71 bp hourly sigma. Post-hoc diagnostic (not registered): matching real and placebo touches on time-into-window leaves the PD/PW effects unchanged (PD 15m 0.177 -> 0.177 in-sample, 0.146 -> 0.151 holdout), so placebo timing is not the source. Named classic setups all fail: PDH/PDL sweep-reclaim fade (H-GEO10) in-sample +0.026 t 1.0 (wrong sign), OR30 breakout (H-GEO11) -0.009 t -0.3 (London +0.11 t 2.0 in-sample, -0.09 holdout), VWAP first cross (H-GEO12) +0.07 t 1.6 / holdout -0.13, round-number hold (H-GEO13) wrong sign: rounds break (+0.05 t 2.9 in, +0.04 holdout), Asia-box Judas sweep (H-GEO14) +0.02 t 0.6. Regime / session dependence (H-GEO15): Wald p < 0.01 in 1 of 30 cell x grouping units; holdout rank rho <= 0 in 11 of 18 testable units -> contradicts holdout.

title: PART: ob200 reducer moved to Rust (crates/at-part), parity exact
body: The Python FlowBook reducer ran at ~20-30% of a core under the current machine load (~15+ min per day for 5 symbols, i.e. ~15 h for 62 days). Wrote crates/at-part (binary part-book, same semantics as participants.FlowBook / reduce_book, 4 Rust unit tests mirroring the Python ones). Parity on BTCUSDT 2025-08-31 (861,389 messages): every flow column and every price/size column identical; depth columns differ by <= 1.1e-7 relative (float32 storage / summation order). 12 s per BTC day vs ~100 s+ in Python. Built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/agent_part, private copy target/agent_part/bin/part-book.exe. No change to the design or the data definition.

title: PART: registered AS_10 lag "of the last minute (known at t)" is not fully known at t
body: H-PART5 baseline B_as lists "AS_10 of the last minute (known at t)". The 10 s markouts of orders in the last 10 s of minute (t-1m, t] end after t, so that value is NOT known at t (look-ahead of up to 10 s). Implemented the point-in-time version instead: AS_10 and AS_60 lags both of the minute (t-2m, t-1m] (AS_60 there was already registered that way). Caught before any fit; noted here so the change is not silent. Also fixed before results: features are clipped at their train-set 0.1/99.9 percentiles and every OLS has symbol intercepts (B and P alike); minutes with fewer than 5 orders have no AS target.

title: STRESS: trades open at the end of the data were dropped (biased no_stop and long-hold units)
body: First draft of the trade layer (stress.walk_signal / walk_bracket) dropped any position still open at the last bar, like post_cascade_study's unresolved trades. Seen in the trial analysis: compression_breakout's no_stop variant averaged -1.19 R because its winners (breakouts that never crossed back through the old box midpoint) were still open and therefore discarded, while every resolved trade was a loser by construction. Fix: open positions are marked to the last close (why = end) in both walkers; the base run is re-run with the fix. The S5 perturbation run (D8) had already started with the old code; it is kept (internally consistent: base and variants drop the same at most one open trade per symbol and variant) and this is stated in the report.

title: GEO part 3: no geometry rule is executable after costs (H-GEO16, H-GEO17)
body: 13 rules (8 deduplicated in-sample BH survivors + 5 named setups) x 16 exit variants, 23 perps, costs pegged 2.0+1.3 bp / taker 5.5+2.0 bp / stops with slippage and gaps / worst-case intrabar / funding. Every rule loses in the purged expanding walk-forward (2023-2026H1): from -0.008 R/trade (PW_HL sweep, n 1389, CI -0.11..+0.09) to -0.104 (PD_HL touch, n 25617); every holdout mean is negative (-0.07 to -0.22 R). 5-minute latency changes little (PD_HL touch -0.094 -> -0.094 in-sample). Alt half-spread on taker legs costs another 0.01-0.03 R. Best exit variant is almost always the 2-sigma stop: wider stops dilute the ~11 bp round-trip cost. Why: the strongest holdout-confirmed effect (prior-day high/low touch continuation, +0.15-0.18 sigma_15m over placebo) is worth +0.01 to +0.02 R GROSS as a stop-entry trade (2 sigma_1h stop, 2R target, 1h time stop) and costs ~0.10 R; with a 1-sigma stop gross is -0.09 R (touches retrace before the tail pays; p_cont 0.46). Optimistic fill-bar ordering does not change this. Versus regime-matched random entries the rules are no better (PD_HL touch -0.018 R [-0.034, -0.001] in-sample; VWAP_S accept +0.037 [+0.016, +0.059] in-sample but +0.008 holdout and still net negative). DSR 0.00 for all (2576 trials). H-GEO16 contradicts both segments. H-GEO17 (liquidation-cluster levels, 16 days holdout only): touch -0.07 t -1.0 on 5337 overlapping events -> contradicts as registered; sweep-and-reclaim of a liquidation cluster reverses (-0.30 t -2.7, n 1813, 16 days) - a single-segment observation for a future registration, not a finding.

title: PART: two pipeline stalls (prefetch guard deadlock, trickling urllib download)
body: 1) The raw-size guard on the prefetch thread (wait while raw >= 1.65 GB) deadlocked on 2025-11-21 (a 1.9 GB day): the main loop joined the prefetch thread of the CURRENT day, which waited for raw to shrink, which needed that day. Fix: an urgent event set before the join disables the guard for the current day. 2) A urllib download of ETHUSDT 2026-10-13 ob200 trickled at ~30 kB/s for 6 min (per-read timeout never fired) while curl got 23 MB/s from the same host. Fix: curl with --speed-limit 300 kB/s over 30 s and retries. Both runs were my own processes, stopped and resumed (atomic per-file writes, so no partial outputs). No effect on data definitions.

title: STRESS results: 1 of 23 units survives every registered stress (zoo_ensemble); trend family fragile, mean-reversion / calendar / shock-desk / setup C proxy fail
body: Pooled base, mean net R/trade [stationary day bootstrap 95% CI], universe L 23 perps, live costs, 4-sigma exchange stop. SURVIVES: zoo_ensemble +0.354 [+0.035, +0.712] (closed trades +0.317, holdout +0.099 n 131); geo_pivot_bo +0.438 [+0.092, +0.835] only with 16 positions open at the data end marked to the last close (closed trades: holdout -0.155 n 71 -> FRAGILE). FRAGILE: tsmom +0.035 [-0.026, +0.103] (also +5 bp flips it), ema_stack +0.064, donchian +0.085, trend_4h +0.099 [-0.024, +0.219] (holdout +0.43 closed n 266), geo_struct +0.116, geo_flag_bo +0.280, shock_regime +0.058 [+0.010, +0.108] but holdout -0.026 (n 618), hrb2 +0.046 (D8 -0.031), compression_breakout (positive only via 17 open trades; closed -0.95), flow_momentum (186 trades), cvd_divergence (1 trade). FAILS: zscore -0.094, rsi -0.052, funding_contrarian -0.021, oi_price_divergence -0.019, weekend_shock_follow -0.051, weekend_drift_fade -0.007, cme_gap_fill -0.115, shock_desk -0.003 (holdout -0.137), hs2_fade_blackout -0.082, setup_c_proxy -0.110. Hypotheses: H-STRESS1 supports (7/9 trend units > 0 under fees x1.5 and +5 bp in both segments), H-STRESS2 supports (5/5 MR+calendar FAIL), H-STRESS3 supports (max 5-min latency cost 0.036 R, shock_desk), H-STRESS4 supports (worst engine-stream crisis window -14.2 R), H-STRESS5 inconclusive (co-stop CVaR +53-56% for compression_breakout, geo_flag_bo), H-STRESS6 supports (P(10 USD day stop) 0 for all; P(3m loss >= 50 USD) <= 1.6%), H-STRESS7 supports (no +-20% cliff in 10 of 11 positive units; the 11th is cvd_divergence with 1 trade), H-STRESS8 contradicts (SBB paths with ~30-day blocks keep the trend edge for 6 of 9), H-STRESS9 contradicts (drought flips tsmom, ema_stack, donchian, shock_regime, compression, hrb2), H-STRESS10 inconclusive (in-sample survivors shock_regime / geo_pivot_bo / zoo_ensemble; holdout -0.026 / +0.401 / +0.664). Surprises: the 10 USD daily stop never binds (3 x 1.30 USD positions); 5-loser runs are certain every quarter for trend units; synthetic bad-year drawdowns are 3-7x a typical historical symbol-year; the hourly gap-fill scenario is a no-op on 24/7 perps (0 gapped stops) while next-open stop fills often help trend units (wicks).

title: PART results: who trades (7 taker types), who is informed, and nothing tradable
body:
Data: 62 days x 5 perps (12 pre-cutoff + 2026-10-06..11-24), 43M+ taker orders, 1 s ob200 books with maker flows. FIT 36 days, HELD 26 days.
H-PART1 inconclusive: rule chose k = 7 (bootstrap ARI 0.86, min BIC among ARI >= 0.8), HELD shares within 3.9 pp of FIT, but k-means agrees only at ARI 0.14 (< 0.5): the GMM split is driven by discrete traits (exact size repeats, significant digits, single vs multi-level).
H-PART2 supports (both segments): 60 s mid-to-mid markout relative to the all-order mean: type 0 tiny round repeaters -1.26 bp FIT / -1.48 HELD, type 1 -0.83/-0.86, type 5 isolated round-size takers -0.93/-1.12 (uninformed); type 6 multi-level burst sweepers +0.84/+0.94 (informed, 55% of notional); |t| 13-23.
H-PART3 (returns) null: HELD dR2 +0.00003 / -0.00005 / -0.0011 at 1/5/60 min; logistic Brier skill < 0. In-sample Wald p ~ 1e-23 meant nothing OOS.
H-PART4 (vol) inconclusive: HELD dR2 +0.0034 [0.0019, 0.0051] (5 min) and +0.0114 [0.0055, 0.0170] (60 min), positive on all 5 symbols, but the FIT-CV gate fails one segment at each horizon.
H-PART5 (adverse selection) contradicts on HELD (dR2 -0.0013, -0.00005) despite FIT-CV +0.018 / +0.006 (AS10); GBM worse than linear.
H-PART6 contradicts: every executable variant net < 0 (taker 5 min -11.5 bp, 60 min -5.3; maker-entry 5 min -9.1, 60 min -2.2; AS quote filter -2.33 bp/fill vs -2.56 unfiltered).
H-PART7 inconclusive (only 2 scored days: xvenue lost Binance flow from 11-23). H-PART8 inconclusive (sweep 1.24x, algo 1.12x; criterion 2x).
Descriptive: liquidation-matched orders (lake, 11-08..11-24, +-5 ms, same side) are 2.9x over-represented in type 3 (mid-size repeated clips).

title: PART: two HMM inputs are price-level artefacts (relative spread, 5 bp near-touch band)
body: The flow-state HMM put 78% of HELD minutes in state 2 vs 25% on FIT. Cause: h_spread = ln spread in bp; for 1-tick markets the relative spread is tick / price, so it moved with the price level (BTC ~110k in 2025 vs ~62k in Nov 2026; median standardised h_spread +4.2 for BTC on HELD). h_cxl / h_refill use the 5 bp near-touch band, whose width in ticks also scales with price (BTC h_cxl +2.0). An ADF/KPSS + PSI check on the HMM inputs (house rule 1.3) would have flagged it; I did not run it before the fit. Fix for a follow-up (new id, not run): spread in ticks, the near-touch band in ticks, PSI check FIT vs HELD before fitting. The type-flow features (shares, signed shares) are scale-free and not affected; the H-PART3..6 verdicts do not hinge on the HMM block (its columns are a minority of P).

title: PART: ablation without the HMM block (descriptive, extra trial, post hoc) corrects the previous entry
body: Correction to the 'price-level artefacts' entry, which said the verdicts do not hinge on the HMM block: partly wrong. Re-running the registered OLS with P minus the HMM columns (hp1, hp2, hchg), same split and bootstrap (4 extra trials, post hoc, not a verdict): ln RV 5 min HELD dR2 +0.00125 [0.00065, 0.00190], FIT-CV +0.00017 (pre-cutoff) / +0.00075 (clean); ln RV 60 min HELD +0.00196 [0.00107, 0.00280], FIT-CV +0.00038 / -0.00051; AS10 HELD +0.00082 [-0.0027, 0.0040]; r5 HELD -0.00002. So most of the registered 60-min RV gain on HELD (+0.0114) came from the drifting HMM state (a price-level / spread-level proxy), while the type-mix-only 5-min RV gain is smaller but positive in every segment. Registered as forward hypothesis H-PART9 (not decided by these numbers). Data: data/research/participants/supervised/ablation_no_hmm.json.

title: TVTP: review of the user tvtp_msvar.py (methodology works on its own synthetic check)
body:
The user's TVTP MS-VAR (repo root tvtp_msvar.py, untracked, left unchanged) runs and recovers its own synthetic DGP: loglik -10592.2, 24 EM iterations, smoothed regime accuracy 0.974, A and Sigma close to truth, W intercepts 4.01 / -3.93 (true 4 / -4), z slopes -3.06 / -2.70 (true -3 / -3). Runtime 4 min 21 s (log-space Python loops).
Review findings, fixed in the copy src/ai_trader/research/tvtp_msvar.py (F1..F13 in its docstring, one regression test each in tests/test_tvtp_msvar.py, 19 tests):
(a) look-ahead: prob_smoothed, pred_ll_ and break_cusum use full-sample parameters (smoothed also future data) - in-sample diagnostics only; forecasts now come from filter_design / walk_forward (params fit on rows < origin, causal filter), regimes Hungarian-aligned across refits (F1, F3).
(b) expected_corr_next used ect_{T-1} (self._X[-1, 1+n*p:]) for x_{T+1}; needs ect_T. Now takes exog_now explicitly and raises when missing (F2).
(c) a regime with ~0 weight got Sigma = 1e-10 I (unbounded likelihood); now inverse-Wishart-type shrinkage with 2 pseudo-obs to the pooled covariance (F4); Cholesky jitter ladder (F5).
(d) random Dirichlet responsibilities per row average out over T rows, so all regimes start at the pooled fit (near a symmetric saddle); added contiguous-block init (F6), original kept as an option.
(e) ll reported was from before the last M-step (F7); BIC count missed K-1 initial-distribution params (F7).
Checked and correct: design lags, z_{t-1} alignment, Kim joint, Zc[1:] with joint[1:] in the logit M-step (a test shows a one-row shift destroys the z effect), gradient, marginal effects (finite differences), CCF (vs a 200k-row simulation).
Parity: with init=dirichlet, cov_prior=0 the copy reproduces the original to 1e-3 in ll and identical parameters, 29x faster (scaled probability-space filter, F11).

title: TVTP design frozen before results
body:
Registered H-TVTP0..H-TVTP6c in research/hypotheses.yaml (block TVTP) before any real-data fit. Data checked for availability only: Bybit XAUUSDT/XAGUSDT 1h and 1d from 2026-03-09 (lake; 24/7 perps, weekend hours kept), flow_3s 3 s candles 2026-11-07..11-26 for metals and crypto, xvenue journal 2026-11-15..11-26 (snapshots every ~3 min), FRED DFII10 / DTWEXBGS / T10YIE (data/research/macro, known_ts = obs + 1 day). The cTrader MCP (127.0.0.1:9876) refused the connection, so there is no long daily metals history: daily (M1d) is registered as underpowered.
Frozen choices: y = log return / EWMA sigma_{t|t-1} (halflife 24 h / 10 d / 60 m), input clipped |y| <= 8, P&L unclipped; ect = rolling 336-row OLS of log XAU on log XAG (hourly), expanding (daily); z hourly = [ect, rv]; z macro = d5 DFII10, d5 log DTWEXBGS, d5 T10YIE (expanding z-scores); spec grid K {2,3} x p {1,2} x {Gaussian, t5} chosen once by validation log score on pre-origin data; walk-forward expanding from 2026-05-01, refit every 336 rows; baselines CTP / VAR / rolling VAR; DM HAC; costs desk = pegged entry 2.0 + 1.3 bp, taker exit 5.5 bp + half measured spread; thresholds {0.5..0.9} picked per fold on fit data; DSR with 40 trials; CUSUM h = 5 vs rolling-corr Fisher-z detector on CPI / NFP / FOMC windows; crypto BTC -> ETH / SOL / DOGE at 1m, entries 3 s after the bar close.
Deviation from the user's design, flagged: Student-t emissions (house rule 1.2) enter only as a selectable spec; the macro drivers are also tried at 1h held at their last known value (M1h-macro, H-TVTP4), because the daily sample is about 240 rows.

title: TVTP M1h: the hourly gold/silver regimes are session / vol states, not leadership states
body:
M1h walk-forward (K=3, p=1, Student-t nu=5 chosen by validation log score; BIC alone would pick K=2 p=1 t5), 15 folds from 2026-05-01. Regime 0: scale 0.16 of the EWMA vol, corr 0.4-0.57, expected duration 60-90 h, occupancy about 24% (= the weekend of a 24/7 perp); regime 1: scale 1.2-1.4, corr 0.85, duration 4-6 h (active / event hours); regime 2: scale 0.55-0.64, corr 0.81, duration 6-10 h. First-lag CCF asymmetries are all below 0.13 in absolute value and below 0.04 after June: no material gold/silver lead-lag at 1h.
TVTP minus constant-TP log score: +0.0055 nats/row (t 1.26) llm_in_sample, +0.0075 (t 2.89) clean_holdout; TVTP minus VAR +0.31..0.34 (t 8-11) - mostly the session/vol structure. Registered H-TVTP1s (post hoc, extra trial) to test against a session-aware VAR before reading anything into the VAR gap.
Lead-lag rule (H-TVTP3): no threshold was net positive on fit data in any fold, so the selected rule never traded; fixed thresholds lose 0.26-0.42 R/trade (t <= -7) in both segments, and the leader roles often fall on the weekend regime.

title: TVTP H-TVTP6a/b: alt open interest is 4h-only in the lake
body: The registered crypto driver was the alt OI 1h log change. The lake (open_interest, venue=bybit) has interval=1h rows for BTCUSDT but only interval=4h for ETHUSDT / SOLUSDT / DOGEUSDT, so the first crypto run failed on an empty frame. Fix: fall back to the 4h interval (latest known 4h log change, expanding z-score) when fewer than 100 1h rows exist. This changes a frozen input before any crypto result was seen; it is recorded with the results.

title: TVTP synthetic Monte Carlo (H-TVTP0): K=2 recovers cleanly; K=3 is at its oracle ceiling; Wald SEs under-cover
body:
50 reps per cell, p=1, l2=0.1, 3 block starts, truth-aligned. K=2 T=4000: filtered accuracy in-sample 0.947, smoothed 0.965, filtered on 1000 fresh rows with frozen params 0.947 (oracle with TRUE params 0.948); A RMSE 0.02-0.036, Sigma RMSE 0.022-0.037, W RMSE 0.33-0.72 (intercepts) / z-slopes recovered in sign 100%; max CCF error median 0.037; no degenerate fits; 20 EM iterations, 8 s. T=1000: OOS accuracy 0.947, CCF error 0.074.
K=3 T=4000: OOS accuracy 0.693 vs oracle 0.709 (the DGP's regimes 0/1 differ only by lag matrix and correlation, so 0.85 was an unattainable bar - my registration error, not estimation error); z-slope signs 98-100%; CCF error median 0.070 (> 0.05); start-to-start ll spread mean 3.7 (multiple starts matter at K=3). T=1000 K=3: sign recovery only 78-88%, CCF error 0.16.
Wald 95% coverage of the z-slopes (soft-count logit Hessian): 0.74-0.84 at K=2, 0.46-0.68 at K=3: use bootstrap CIs, never these SEs.
Init: blocks vs the original Dirichlet (10 reps each) are indistinguishable on accuracy and ll; F6 is harmless but was not needed on these DGPs.
H-TVTP0 verdict by the registered rule: inconclusive (K=2 passes all three, K=3 fails accuracy and CCF).
Synthetic CUSUM (30 reps, unmodelled correlation-flip regime for 200 rows): CUSUM hit 100%, median delay 2.5 rows, 3.6 false alarms / 1000 rows; rolling-correlation detector hit 97%, delay 19 rows, 5.1 false / 1000.

title: TVTP gold/silver hourly (M1h): better density forecasts than any VAR, but from session/vol states; no lead-lag; nothing tradable
body:
Spec K=3 p=1 t5 (validation log score; BIC picks K=2 p=1 t5). 15 expanding folds from 2026-05-01; test rows 1464 llm_in_sample, 3552 clean_holdout.
H-TVTP1 log score (nats/row, HAC t): TVTP-CTP +0.0055 (1.26) in-sample, +0.0075 (2.89) holdout; TVTP-VAR +0.339 (8.2) / +0.308 (11.4); TVTP-RVAR +0.350 / +0.317. Registered rule: supports in clean_holdout (in-sample segment alone: inconclusive).
H-TVTP1s (post hoc): an hour-of-week-scaled t5 VAR (SVAR) closes about 0.23 of the 0.31 gap. Holdout TVTP-SVAR +0.080 (t 4.45) overall, but weekday rows -0.006 (t -0.58) and weekend rows +0.280 (t 6.1); TVTP-CTP on weekdays +0.0085 (t 2.89). Rule: supports - read as: on weekdays the regime model is no better than a calendar-scaled VAR; the z drivers add a small, significant gain over constant transitions.
H-TVTP2 covariance: holdout QLIKE TVTP 0.240, CTP 0.325, rolling120 1.194, EWMA 1.138, DCC 1.152 (TVTP minus each t -8.8 to -10.8; vs CTP t -3.4); cov-element MSE also lower (t -6 to -7.5); in-sample same ordering (t -2.4 to -3.2). Supports in both segments; the baselines are blind to the weekend scale collapse, which is most of the gap.
H-TVTP3 lead-lag rule: no threshold was net positive on fit data in any fold -> zero trades (registered verdict: inconclusive, n < 30). Fixed thresholds 0.5-0.9 in the holdout: net -0.26..-0.36 R/trade (t -9.7..-13.6), gross -0.02..+0.03 R (|t| <= 1.3); weekend gross +0.025..+0.042 R (t 1.4-2.2) against about 0.3 R of costs. Desk costs about 9.9 bp on XAG (pegged 3.3 + taker 5.5 + half spread 1.05).
H-TVTP5 CUSUM (13 holdout CPI/NFP/FOMC episodes): hit rate 0.31 both; delay 1.25 h vs 19 h; false alarms 7.4 vs 10.5 per 1000 rows; but binomial p vs chance 0.17 -> inconclusive (in-sample 5 episodes: 0.4 vs 0.2, p 0.26, inconclusive).
Regimes (fold 14): weekend scale 0.16 corr 0.39 duration 62 h; event scale 1.2 corr 0.85 duration 5.6 h; normal scale 0.55 corr 0.80 duration 5.8 h; first-lag CCF asymmetry |.| < 0.03.

title: TVTP drivers (H-TVTP4, H-TVTP4d) and daily (H-TVTP1d): real yields and the dollar do not drive switching stably
body:
H-TVTP4 (M1h-macro, K=3 p=1 t5, fit separately per subperiod, 30 parametric bootstrap reps each, regimes aligned): AME on the leave hazard, 95% CI excluding 0 - d5 DFII10: none in llm_in_sample; in clean_holdout weekend regime -0.078 and event regime +0.057 (opposite signs across regimes, not replicated in-sample); d5 DTWEXBGS: none in either; d5 T10YIE: none. Verdict inconclusive. The price-based rv state is the stable driver: normal-regime leave hazard -0.089 / -0.083 (both CIs exclude 0), weekend regime -0.034 / -0.054 (both exclude 0).
M1d (Bybit daily since 2026-03, 148 holdout rows, K=2 p=1): TVTP-CTP +0.013 (t 0.18), TVTP-VAR -0.044 (t -0.56), TVTP-RVAR +0.095 (t 0.83): inconclusive, underpowered. H-TVTP4d full-sample daily AME CIs all include 0: contradicts (weak evidence by construction).

title: TVTP gold/silver 1m from flow_3s (H-TVTP3b): TVTP worse than constant transitions; rule never trades
body: 12441 valid 1m rows 2026-11-07..11-25 (collector gaps; segments respected), spec K=3 p=1 Gaussian, 6 rolling folds (4320-row window) from 2026-11-13. Log score TVTP-CTP -0.0145 (t -2.67), TVTP-VAR +0.485 (t 12.3) - again vol states (scales 0.24 / 0.77 / 2.0). First-lag CCF asymmetry |.| < 0.05. Rule: no threshold net positive on fit data in any fold (fit means -1.4..-2.5 R), zero trades: inconclusive by rule; fixed thresholds lose 1.5-2.2 R/trade in the holdout (t -22..-37).
